newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: "Sensibly priced" A$ value helps exports -minister.
newsitem.headline: "Sensibly priced" A$ value helps exports -minister.

text.p: Australian Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said on Monday a "sensibly priced" Australian dollar would boost exports and would be welcomed by rural industries and exporters.
"A sensibly-priced dollar always helps exports and is always welcome in the bush," he told reporters, when asked if the weaker dollar would help exports.
Anderson made the comments ahead of his departure for Washington on Monday for talks on agricultural issues.
Deputy Prime Minister and National Party Leader Tim Fischer has previously said that a more accurate level of the Australian dollar would help exporters.
Four cuts in official interest rates since July last year has seen the Australian dollar shed about eight U.S. cents in value since it hit a high of US$0.82 late last year.
The Australian dollar was trading around US$0.7385 at 0100 GMT (11.00 a.m.) on Monday morning.
